title: BYD’s answer to its car-sales slump: a humanoid robot in every showroom

content_html:
BYD sells more electric cars than anyone. Next month, it wants to sell you one using a robot.

China’s biggest EV maker will unveil its first humanoid robot in August, at its Di Space experience centres in Zhengzhou, the company told the South China Morning Post. It will be a working prototype, not a concept, and it will mingle with visitors.

The robot reportedly has a name and a job. According to Chinese outlet KrASIA, citing a since-deleted BYD post, it is called “Xiao Di,” a service humanoid that stands 1.61 metres, weighs 58.5kg and can translate between six Chinese dialects and six foreign languages in real time. BYD has not officially confirmed the specs.

Cars first, then everything else

The plan starts in the showroom. Executive vice-president Stella Li wants two or three robots in every BYD store, greeting customers and explaining cars. She insists they will assist human staff, not replace them.

From there, the ambition widens: supermarkets, malls and warehouses in the medium term, and eventually homes, doing the cleaning, cooking and companionship. BYD says it will build an open platform that makes both its own robots and models co-developed with others.

Its pitch is manufacturing. BYD already builds its own batteries, motors and electronics at huge scale, and Li argues cars and robots share the same roots. That, in theory, lets it build robots more cheaply than a standalone startup can.

Everyone with a car factory wants one

BYD is not early. It is late. Tesla’s Optimus is the headline rival, but China’s carmakers are swarming in. Xpeng is trialling its Iron robot, Li Auto is exploring designs, and Chery’s Aimoga is already selling to consumers.

The backdrop is a humanoid boom. China made about 20,000 humanoids in 2025 and more than 40,000 in the first half of 2026 alone, with the government pushing for far more. Some forecasts stretch to tens of millions of robot workers within a decade.

The catch, and the timing

There is a reason for the robot rush, and it is not entirely rosy. BYD’s car business is under strain, with first-half sales down about 16% amid China’s brutal price war. A new growth story is welcome.

But a slick demo is not a business. Investors still have no price, no production timeline and no paid deployments to judge. BYD has also denied separate reports of a factory robot line, so much remains unconfirmed.

And the overseas door is closing. The move lands just as the US moves to bar imports of Chinese robots, which could keep Xiao Di out of one of its biggest potential markets. For now, BYD’s robot has one job: sell cars, in China, from a showroom floor.

content_html_zh:
比亚迪的电动汽车销量比任何人都多。 下个月，它想向你出售一个使用机器人的产品。

该公司告诉《南华早报》，中国最大的电动汽车制造商将于 8 月在郑州的 Di Space 体验中心推出首款人形机器人。 它将是一个工作原型，而不是一个概念，它将与参观者打成一片。

据报道，该机器人有名字和工作。 据中国媒体 KrASIA 援引已被删除的比亚迪帖子报道，它被称为“小迪”，是一种服务人形机器人，身高 1.61 米，重 58.5 公斤，可以实时翻译六种中国方言和六种外语。 比亚迪尚未正式确认该规格。

首先是汽车，然后是其他一切

该计划从陈列室开始。 执行副总裁李斯特希望每个比亚迪商店都配备两到三个机器人，负责迎接顾客并解释汽车。 她坚称他们将帮助人类员工，而不是取代他们。

从那时起，野心不断扩大：中期是超市、购物中心和仓库，最终是家庭，负责清洁、烹饪和陪伴。 比亚迪表示，将建立一个开放平台，让自己的机器人和模型与其他公司共同开发。

它的主旨是制造。 比亚迪已经大规模生产自己的电池、电机和电子产品，李认为汽车和机器人有着相同的根源。 从理论上讲，这使得它比独立初创公司更便宜地制造机器人。

每个拥有汽车工厂的人都想要一辆

比亚迪也不早了。 现在已经晚了。 特斯拉的擎天柱是主要竞争对手，但中国汽车制造商正在蜂拥而至。 小鹏汽车正在试验其 Iron 机器人，理想汽车正在探索设计，奇瑞的 Aimoga 已经向消费者销售。

背景是人形生物的繁荣。 中国在 2025 年生产了约 20,000 个人形机器人，仅在 2026 年上半年就生产了 40,000 多个，而且政府还在推动更多。 一些预测在十年内将有数千万机器人工人。

收获和时机

机器人热潮是有原因的，但也不完全是乐观的。 比亚迪的汽车业务面临压力，由于中国残酷的价格战，上半年销量下降了约16%。 欢迎新的成长故事。

但精美的演示并不是一门生意。 投资者仍然没有价格、没有生产时间表、也没有付费部署来判断。 比亚迪还否认了有关工厂机器人生产线的单独报道，因此许多内容尚未得到证实。

海外大门正在关闭。 此举恰逢美国禁止进口中国机器人之际，这可能会使小迪无法进入其最大的潜在市场之一。 目前，比亚迪的机器人只有一项工作：在中国的展厅里销售汽车。
